title: Building a Responsive Layout System knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “Building a Responsive Layout System” in Dart Sass?
options: The design problem is usually consistency across many related styles, not the ability to write shorter syntax. Combine semantic tokens, a clear module boundary, reusable component patterns, and CSS-native runtime features where each has a distinct role.
The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.
questions.answer_key: The design problem is usually consistency across many related styles, not the ability to write shorter syntax. Combine semantic tokens, a clear module boundary, reusable component patterns, and CSS-native runtime features where each has a distinct role.
questions.explanation: The design problem is usually consistency across many related styles, not the ability to write shorter syntax. Combine semantic tokens, a clear module boundary, reusable component patterns, and CSS-native runtime features where each has a distinct role. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “Defining container tokens”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
Choose the variable scope and name for the decision it represents. Test default and overridden values so a new configuration does not silently change unrelated components.
questions.answer_key: Choose the variable scope and name for the decision it represents. Test default and overridden values so a new configuration does not silently change unrelated components.
questions.explanation: Choose the variable scope and name for the decision it represents. Test default and overridden values so a new configuration does not silently change unrelated components. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.

questions.prompt: Which review decision most directly supports maintainability for “Building a Responsive Layout System”?
options: Treat successful compilation as proof that the interface is accessible and behaves correctly in every browser.
Expose internal implementation details as public API and postpone documentation until after release.
Design the public interface for the next developer: document tokens and arguments, keep internals private, compile from a documented entrypoint, and demonstrate the result in a small consumer page.
Generate every possible selector or theme combination, even when most variants are never used.
questions.answer_key: Design the public interface for the next developer: document tokens and arguments, keep internals private, compile from a documented entrypoint, and demonstrate the result in a small consumer page.
questions.explanation: Design the public interface for the next developer: document tokens and arguments, keep internals private, compile from a documented entrypoint, and demonstrate the result in a small consumer page. The other choices increase output, assume unverified behavior, or make the public interface harder to maintain.
